edges.description: The variant destabilises the neuroserpin fold.
The destabilised protein polymerises by loop-sheet linkage.
Polymerized/retained neuroserpin can no longer inhibit tPA.
Inclusion load triggers a Ca2+-dependent ER overload response.
Inclusion load disrupts ER-mitochondria contacts and mitochondrial function.
Inclusion-body formation is sufficient to drive neurodegeneration.
Sustained ER overload contributes to neuronal death.
Mitochondrial injury contributes to neuronal death.
Unchecked tPA activity contributes to cortical hyperexcitability and seizures.
Cortical (especially frontal) neuronal loss produces progressive dementia.
Neuronal loss produces cortical atrophy in severe disease.
Subcortical neuronal dysfunction produces involuntary movements.
Frontal cortical involvement produces a dysexecutive syndrome.
Age- and dose-dependent neuronal accumulation of mutant neuroserpin.
edges.limitations: An overexpression transgene rather than a knock-in, and accumulation requires homozygous high expression.

nodes.description: Preclinical: the small molecule embelin destabilises neuroserpin conformers and impairs polymerization in vitro; it is not a clinical therapy.

nodes.description: The most destabilising variant; severe childhood/adolescent progressive myoclonus epilepsy, and can arise de novo.
